rephrased_fields.P:
Fix the INI config string handling introduced in Ansible 2.15. Right now, string values loaded from INI config files like `ansible.cfg` come back with the surrounding quotes still attached instead of being unquoted. That affects any string config set in INI files, so playbooks and modules that expect plain strings can break because the literal quotes are included in the value.
Quotes are currently preserved for strings coming from INI files:
``` 
ANSIBLE_COW_PATH(/tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg) = "/usr/bin/cowsay" 
CONFIG_FILE() = /tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg 
DEFAULT_MANAGED_STR(/tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg) = "foo bar baz" 
```

Make sure string values read from INI files automatically strip a single outer pair of matching single or double quotes during type coercion when the declared type is `"str"`.
Make `get_config_value_and_origin` return the value together with its origin details when the value comes from an INI file.
Update `ensure_type` so it handles values from INI files by unquoting them when the detected origin type is `ini`.
Make `get_config_value_and_origin` use `ensure_type` to enforce the right type for config values coming from INI files.
rephrased_fields.D:
Return unquoted strings for values loaded from INI files:
``` 
ANSIBLE_COW_PATH(/tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg) = /usr/bin/cowsay 
CONFIG_FILE() = /tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg 
DEFAULT_MANAGED_STR(/tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg) = foo bar baz 
```

Remove only one outer pair of matching quotes, either single `'...'` or double `"..."`, and leave inner quotes alone.
Add an `origin_ftype` parameter to the `ensure_type` function signature so it can decide when unquoting should happen.
If a value has multiple layers of quotes, unquote only one outer layer at a time and preserve anything inside. Handle both single ('...') and double ("...") quotes consistently for every source, including INI files, environment variables, and YAML.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Create a temporary INI file `/tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg`: 
``` 
[defaults] cowpath = "/usr/bin/cowsay" ansible_managed = "foo bar baz" 
``` 
2. Run: 
```
 ansible-config dump -c /tmp/ansible_quoted.cfg --only-changed 
```
rephrased_fields.A:
This only affects strings coming from INI files. Environment variables and other config sources are not affected.
The bug shows up when dumping or reading config values through `ansible-config` or through plugins that depend on config lookups.

rephrased_fields.P:
Remove the broken `ansible-galaxy login` flow. It no longer works because the GitHub API used for authentication has been shut down. That command used the discontinued GitHub OAuth Authorizations API for interactive GitHub auth during role and collection publishing.

Switch users to API token-based auth from the Galaxy portal instead.

Right now, `ansible-galaxy login` fails with cryptic or confusing errors and gives no clear next step.

- Completely remove the `ansible-galaxy login` submodule by deleting the `login.py` file and all related functionality.
- Update the Galaxy API error message to point users to the new auth options: token file or `--token` parameter.
rephrased_fields.D:
When `ansible-galaxy role login` is run, show a clear error that says the login command has been removed and explain how to use API tokens instead. Include where to get the token: https://galaxy.ansible.com/me/preferences, and explain the CLI options for passing it in.

- Add validation in the Galaxy CLI to catch attempts to use the removed login command and show an informative error message with the replacement options.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Try to execute ansible-galaxy role login
2. Observe that the command fails or produces an error
rephrased_fields.A: ansible-galaxy, galaxy.api, galaxy.login

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix the SSH connection plugin so it always pull its options from the right config sources. Right now, some documented settings under the `ssh_connection` scope get ignored, and reset behavior is inconsistent.

The reset logic checks for an active persistent connection with parameters that do not match the ones the plugin actually used. That causes wrong socket detection and inconsistent reset behavior.

Some SSH options defined in the configuration are not getting applied because they are not resolved through the plugin's option system. The reset routine may also check for a socket with hardcoded or default parameters that differ from the real connection parameters, which causes missed detections or unnecessary stop attempts.

- Resolve SSH connection configuration through `get_option()` using normal Ansible precedence (CLI, config, environment, inventory/vars). Produce one effective runtime value per option.
- Use those resolved effective values for every SSH runtime decision, including command construction, file transfer selection, retry behavior, and persistent connection management, no matter where the value came from.
- Before resetting a persistent SSH connection, check whether a persistent socket exists using the same effective parameters that created it. If no socket exists, emit a debug message and skip the stop action. If a socket exists, perform the stop action.
- Make `transfer_method` control file transfer behavior, including fallback and retries when applicable, using the same precedence rules as the other options.
- Stop defining SSH-specific options in core configuration, including `ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS`, `ANSIBLE_SCP_IF_SSH`, `ANSIBLE_SSH_RETRIES`, `ANSIBLE_SSH_CONTROL_PATH`, `ANSIBLE_SSH_CONTROL_PATH_DIR`, `ANSIBLE_SSH_EXECUTABLE`, `DEFAULT_SFTP_BATCH_MODE`, and `DEFAULT_SSH_TRANSFER_METHOD`. Resolve those behaviors inside the SSH connection plugin using the standard precedence.
rephrased_fields.D:
Resolve SSH connection options through the standard Ansible precedence (CLI, config, environment, inventory/ or vars) with `get_option()`. Use the same effective parameters during reset that the active connection used to decide whether a persistent socket exists before trying to stop it.

- If only a CLI value is provided, use that as the effective setting.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Define SSH options under `ssh_connection` in a configuration source. 
2. Run anything that triggers an SSH connection and file transfer. 
3. Observe that the options are not applied in command construction and execution.
4. Invoke connection reset and meta reset, and observe the mismatch between socket detection and the actual connection parameters.
rephrased_fields.A: - Support and resolve the following SSH-related options through that precedence: `ssh_common_args`, `sftp_extra_args`, `scp_extra_args`, `ssh_extra_args`, `ssh_args`, `ssh_executable`, `control_path`, `control_path_dir`, `timeout`, `private_key_file`, `remote_user`, `retries`, `transfer_method`, `scp_if_ssh`, and `sftp_batch_mode`.

rephrased_fields.P:
Add a real offline mode to `ansible-galaxy collection install` for local tarballs.

Right now, installing a collection from a local tarball in a network-isolated environment still makes `ansible-galaxy` try to contact Galaxy during dependency resolution. That happens even when the dependency already exists in `collections_paths`. Make local-tarball installs work fully offline by using only local tarballs and already installed dependencies, with no calls to any distribution server. This applies only to local tarball artifacts, not collections from remote Git repositories or URLs that point to remote tarballs.

`ansible-galaxy` currently reaches out to the Galaxy API during dependency resolution and fails offline even when the required dependency is already available locally.
### Example Output
```

Starting galaxy collection install process

Found installed collection amazon.aws:3.1.1 at '/root/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/amazon/aws'

Process install dependency map

Initial connection to default Galaxy server

Calling Galaxy API for collection versions

ERROR! Unknown error when attempting to call Galaxy API (network is unreachable)
```

- Add a boolean `--offline` flag to the `ansible-galaxy collection install` subcommand, defaulting to `False`. The help text must be exactly: “Install collection artifacts (tarballs) without contacting any distribution servers. This does not apply to collections in remote Git repositories or URLs to remote tarballs.”
- Propagate `--offline` through the install flow as an `offline` boolean parameter and make these interfaces honor it: `download_collections(..., offline=False)`, `install_collections(..., offline)`, `_resolve_depenency_map(..., offline)`, `build_collection_dependency_resolver(..., offline=False)`, and the `MultiGalaxyAPIProxy(..., offline=False)` constructor.
- In `--offline` mode, make dependency resolution and installation avoid all network access and use only locally installed collections and/or local tarballs. Anything that depends on remote data, like version metadata or signatures, must be unavailable in this mode and must not trigger requests to distribution servers.
- In `--offline` mode, make remote version fetching/listing behave as if there are no remote results, with no network traffic at all, so resolution uses only local information.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make installs from local tarballs stay fully offline and never contact any distribution server. If the dependency is already installed locally, continue the install offline and print that the dependency is already installed and skipped. Finish installing the target collection successfully with no network calls. This is only expected for local tarball artifacts, not collections from remote Git repositories or remote tarball URLs.

- When `--offline` is not used, keep the current behavior, including contacting configured Galaxy servers. If the configured server is unreachable, the error must include exactly: `ERROR! Unknown error when attempting to call Galaxy at '{{ offline_server }}'`, showing the configured URL exactly as configured.
- In `--offline` mode, if a required local dependency is missing, fail the install without any network attempts, and include exactly:
`ERROR! Failed to resolve the requested dependencies map. Could not satisfy the following requirements:\n* ns.coll2:>=1.0.0 (dependency of ns.coll1:1.0.0)`
- In `--offline` mode, if required dependencies are already available locally or supplied as local tarballs, complete successfully and output exactly these lines as appropriate: "ns.coll1:1.0.0 was installed successfully", "ns.coll1:2.0.0 was installed successfully", "ns.coll2:2.0.0 was installed successfully".
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Install a dependency from a local tarball:
```bash

$ ansible-galaxy collection install amazon-aws-3.1.1.tar.gz

Starting galaxy collection install process

Process install dependency map

Starting collection install process

Installing 'amazon.aws:3.1.1' to '/root/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/amazon/aws'

amazon.aws:3.1.1 was installed successfully

```
2. Then install another collection from a local tarball that depends on the one above, in an environment without internet:

Calling Galaxy API for collection versions

rephrased_fields.P:
Handle the cryptographic identity reset flow so it shows progress right away and blocks duplicate actions.

Right now, when resetting a cryptographic identity on an account with a large number of keys (for example, ≥20k) and an existing backup, the flow starts with a long delay and shows no visible feedback. During that delay, the “Continue” button stays active, so it can be clicked multiple times. That kicks off overlapping flows and multiple password prompts, which leaves the session in a broken state.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make the reset flow behave like this:

- Show immediate visual feedback that the reset has started (for example, spinner/progress).

- Show clear guidance not to close or refresh the page during the process.

- Lock the UI or disable controls so repeated submissions and overlapping flows cannot happen.

- Show exactly one password prompt for the reset flow.

- The file `ResetIdentityPanel.tsx` should import `InlineSpinner` and introduce a local `inProgress` state via `useState(false)` to track the active reset operation.

- The primary “Continue” button should set "inProgress" to true immediately on click, before awaiting the async call to `matrixClient.getCrypto()?.resetEncryption(...)`, ensuring the UI reflects progress without delay and preventing duplicate submissions.

- While "inProgress" is true, the “Continue” button must be rendered in a disabled state (via the existing Button’s disabled prop) and must not introduce extra attributes like `aria-busy`; the only observable change on the button is its disabled state and its content swap described below.

- The content of the “Continue” button must switch to an inline composition of <InlineSpinner /> followed by the exact text "Reset in progress...", rendered as adjacent inline content inside the button without adding new wrapper elements or changing surrounding layout containers.

- A warning message with the exact text Do not close this window until the reset is finished must be rendered only while "inProgress" is true, and must appear within an element carrying the class mx_ResetIdentityPanel_warning.

- The “Cancel” button should be rendered in the initial (idle) state and must be replaced by the warning message described above when inProgress is true, so that only one of them appears at any given time.

- Aside from the button’s disabled state and the conditional rendering described, the surrounding `EncryptionCard` structure, headings, and list content must remain unchanged to avoid incidental DOM churn.

- The click handler for “Continue” must await the completion of `resetEncryption((makeRequest) => uiAuthCallback(matrixClient, makeRequest))` and invoke the provided onFinish(evt) callback exactly once after the asynchronous operation resolves.

- No additional ARIA attributes, role changes, or structural wrappers should be introduced in this component beyond what is specified here; the intent is to surface progress visually and disable repeat actions without altering existing markup semantics.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Sign in with an account that has ≥20,000 keys cached and uploaded to an existing backup.

2. Navigate to **Settings → Encryption**.

3. Click **Reset cryptographic identity**.

4. Click **Continue** (optionally, click it multiple times during the initial delay).
rephrased_fields.A:
- There is no visible feedback for ~15–20 seconds after clicking **Continue**.

- The **Continue** button stays clickable, so multiple submissions can happen.

- Multiple concurrent flows trigger repeated password prompts.

- Overlapping reset attempts can leave the session in a broken state.

rephrased_fields.P:
Don't require a DB for auth when only using JWT and non-DB flag storage.

When Flipt uses JWT auth and a non-database storage backend for flag state, like OCI, Git, or Local, it still tries to connect to a database even though it doesn't need one. Fix that behavior so JWT auth with non-DB storage does not require any database connection.

Add a field to `AuthenticationMethodInfo` that tells whether each auth method needs a database connection. Name that field `RequiresDatabase`, and set it explicitly for every supported authentication method in the config.
rephrased_fields.D:
Don't let Flipt try to connect to a database when using JWT authentication with a non-database storage backend. Only authentication methods that need persistent storage, like static token auth, should trigger a database connection.

- For JWT authentication, set `RequiresDatabase` to `false`, since JWT does not need a database connection to work.
- For authentication methods including static token, OIDC, GitHub, and Kubernetes, set `RequiresDatabase` to `true`, since those methods rely on persistent database storage.
- Add a method on `AuthenticationConfig`, such as `RequiresDatabase()`, that returns `true` if any enabled authentication method in its `Methods` map requires a database connection, and `false` otherwise. Only consider enabled methods and their `RequiresDatabase` property.
- During startup, make the authentication service initialization logic in `authenticationGRPC` use the value returned by `RequiresDatabase()` to decide whether to create a database connection for authentication. If no enabled authentication method requires a database, run without trying to initialize or connect to one.
- In the authentication service cleanup routine (`Run` in `AuthenticationService`), skip execution for any authentication method where `RequiresDatabase` is `false`, even if cleanup is otherwise configured for that method.
- Update `ShouldRunCleanup` in `AuthenticationConfig` so it checks both whether a method is enabled and whether it requires a database connection. Return `true` only for enabled methods that require a database and have cleanup configured.
- Wire any database-requirement changes all the way through config and service initialization so every combination of enabled auth methods and storage backends behaves correctly.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Configure Flipt to use a non-database storage backend (e.g., OCI, Git, or Local).

2.  Enable JWT authentication as the only authentication method.

3.  Start the Flipt service.

4.  Observe that Flipt tries to connect to a database even though only JWT auth and non-DB storage are used.
rephrased_fields.A:
- Some authentication methods, like static token auth, do require a database, but JWT does not.

- Cache is not relevant here, since everything is already in memory with these storage backends.

- The current code paths show that the check is too broad and does not handle the JWT + non-DB storage case correctly.

- Make sure authentication method configuration reflects database dependencies accurately. For example, when using OCI, Git, or Local storage and JWT is the only enabled authentication method, Flipt should never try to connect to a database.

rephrased_fields.P:
Make the OFREP bulk evaluation endpoint work when `context.flags` is missing.

Using the OFREP client provider with flipt mostly works great, but bulk evaluation currently breaks when the request does not include the `flags` context key. In that case, the endpoint returns an error, which does not match how this endpoint should work. When no explicit flag list is provided, the client should load all relevant flags for synchronous evaluation.

The request currently fails with: `{"errorCode":"INVALID_CONTEXT","errorDetails":"flags were not provided in context"}`

- Update the OFREP bulk evaluation endpoint in `internal/server/ofrep/evaluation.go` to accept requests without the `context.flags` key. Do not treat a missing key as an error.
- If listing flags for the namespace fails, return a gRPC error with code `Internal` and message `failed to fetch list of flags`.
- Remove the old error path that returned `{"errorCode":"INVALID_CONTEXT","errorDetails":"flags were not provided in context"}`. Do not emit an error just because `context.flags` is missing.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make the request succeed when `flags` is not provided. Evaluate and return results for the available flags in the current namespace, using the provided context, including `targetingKey` and the namespace header. Return the same kind of response as a normal bulk evaluation for those flags.

- When `context.flags` is present, treat it as a comma-separated string of flag keys. Trim surrounding whitespace from each key before evaluation, and evaluate only the listed keys.
- When `context.flags` is absent, resolve the namespace from request metadata or headers, for example `X-Flipt-Namespace`. If no namespace is provided, default to `default`.
- When `context.flags` is absent, list flags for the resolved namespace through an injected store dependency and evaluate only flags of type `BOOLEAN_FLAG_TYPE` and flags of type `VARIANT_FLAG_TYPE` with `Enabled == true`.
- Make sure each evaluated flag returned from bulk evaluation includes its `key`, `variant` (string), `value` (typed), and `metadata` fields. The structure must match the OFREP bulk response used by the system.
rephrased_fields.R: Send a bulk evaluation request without `context.flags`, for example: ``` curl --request POST \ --url https://try.flipt.io/ofrep/v1/evaluate/flags \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Accept: application/json' \ --header 'X-Flipt-Namespace: default' \ --data '{ "context": { "targetingKey": "targetingKey1" } }' ``` Or use the OFREP client provider for bulk evaluation without specifying `flags` in the context.
rephrased_fields.A:

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix a bug in CORS `allowed_origins` parsing.

Fields that should decode into string slices, like `allowed_origins`, are currently only split on commas. Restore support for values separated by whitespace too, including spaces and newlines. Right now, if origins are provided with spaces or repeated whitespace, the config gets parsed wrong and the whole string can end up as one entry.

- In `internal/config/config.go`, make any `[]string` field that comes from a scalar string split on all whitespace characters, including spaces, tabs, and newlines.
- If the input string is empty, decode it as an empty slice (`[]`), not `nil` and not a slice with an empty string.
- Make the string-to-slice decode hook run only when the source value is a string and the target type is `[]string`. If the source value is already an array/sequence or is not a string, leave it unchanged.
rephrased_fields.D:
Parse `allowed_origins` space-separated values as separate entries. For the example above, the parsed config should be:

```

json ["foo.com", "bar.com", "baz.com"] 

``` 

- Treat multiple consecutive whitespace characters as a single separator, and ignore leading or trailing whitespace in the resulting slice.
- For `cors.allowed_origins`, the YAML value `allowed_origins: "foo.com bar.com  baz.com"` must decode to `CorsConfig.AllowedOrigins == []string{"foo.com", "bar.com",  "baz.com"}`, keeping the original item order.
- Apply the same splitting behavior to environment variable input too, so equivalent whitespace-separated values from ENV decode exactly the same as YAML.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Set `cors.allowed_origins` in `advanced.yml` like this:

``` yaml

cors: 

    enabled: true 

    allowed_origins: "foo.com bar.com baz.com"

``` 

2. Start Flipt with this config.
3. Check the parsed `AllowedOrigins` value.
rephrased_fields.A:
- Restore the previous behavior. This started regressing after the config handling changed.
- This mainly impacts CORS origin parsing, where whitespace-separated values are commonly used in config files.

rephrased_fields.P:
Make the Flipt audit logfile sink handle setup and writes correctly.

Initialize the logfile audit sink successfully whether the target file already exists or not. Create missing parent directories automatically. Surface clear, distinct errors when directory checks fail, directory creation fails, or file open fails. Write audits as newline-delimited JSON, one JSON object per line, and close the sink cleanly.

Right now, starting Flipt with an audit log path whose parent directory does not exist fails during sink initialization because the code does not create the directory first and the file open returns “no such file or directory.” The current flow only tries to open the file directly, so directory-check and directory-creation failures are not handled separately. There is also no verification that emitted audit events are newline-terminated JSON lines.

- `newSink(logger, path, fs)` should check the parent directory of `path`; if it’s missing, create it, then open/create the logfile for append; if it exists, open for append. 
-`newSink` should return distinguishable, descriptive errors for each failing operation: directory check, directory creation, and file open. 
- `SendAudits` should emit one JSON object per event, newline-terminated, to the underlying file handle. 
- `Sink.Close()` should succeed after initialization and after writing. 
- `Sink.String()` should return the sink type identifier: `logfile`.
rephrased_fields.D:
- If the log path’s parent directory does not exist, create it and then open or create the log file. 
- If the file already exists, open it for append. 
- Return explicit errors when checking the directory, creating it, or opening the file fails. 
- Sending an event should write a single newline-terminated JSON object to the file. 
- Closing the sink should succeed without errors.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Configure an audit logfile path whose parent directory does not exist (for example, `/tmp/flipt/audit/audit.log`). 
2. Ensure the parent directory (e.g., `/tmp/flipt/audit`) is absent. 
3. Start Flipt and observe initialization fails with a file-open error rather than creating the directory.
rephrased_fields.A:
- Provide a `filesystem` abstraction exposing `OpenFile`, `Stat`, and `MkdirAll`, plus a concrete `osFS` used in success-path construction. 
- Use a `file` abstraction (write/close and `Name()`), and make `Sink` hold that handle instead of a concrete `*os.File` so tests can inject an in-memory implementation.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix EC2 detection in Teleport. The current check is too loose and returns false positives because it does a simple HTTP GET to the EC2 metadata endpoint and never validates the response body. If something on the network, like a captive portal, intercepts the request and sends back HTTP 200 with its own content, such as a login page or redirect page, Teleport wrongly decides it is running on EC2.

That breaks EC2 tag-based discovery in a pretty bad way. Once Teleport thinks it is on EC2, it tries to read EC2 tags to figure out the node hostname. Since it gets HTML instead of real metadata, it ends up using that HTML as the hostname.

On non-EC2 nodes behind a captive portal, `tsh ls` and the Web UI show the node name as raw HTML. The debug logs show Teleport misidentifying the node as EC2 and parsing the HTML response as the `TeleportHostname` tag.

- Update `NewInstanceMetadataClient` to accept optional configuration parameters so the created client can be customized at instantiation time.
- Update `IsAvailable` on `InstanceMetadataClient` to check availability by fetching the EC2 instance ID within a short timeout, like 250ms, and validating it against the expected EC2 instance ID format.
- Remove direct HTTP requests to the EC2 metadata endpoint from the availability check, and rely on the internal metadata retrieval method instead to improve efficiency and reduce latency.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make the EC2 availability check actually verify EC2 metadata. Don’t treat any successful HTTP response as proof that the host is on EC2. Fetch the instance ID and validate that it matches a real EC2 instance ID format, like `i-1a2b3c4d` or `i-1234567890abcdef0`. That prevents false positives on captive-portal networks and stops on-prem nodes from being misidentified as EC2, so they keep reporting the correct hostname.

- Support passing configuration options as functional arguments when creating the client, so internal dependencies or behavior can be customized dynamically.
- Add a way to provide a custom internal metadata client implementation through those creation options to control how metadata gets retrieved.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix MARC records incorrectly matching existing ISBN-based "promise item" edition records.

Some MARC records are getting matched to existing ISBN-based "promise item" edition records in the catalog when they should not. That corrupts data because incomplete or wrong metadata from the MARC records can overwrite records that were previously entered manually or matched correctly by ISBN.

The current behavior looks too permissive, especially around title-based matching, even when existing records already have ISBNs. The matching system is not evaluating metadata deeply or consistently across different import flows.

This can affect a wide range of imported records, especially records with incomplete metadata that happen to share a common title with an existing ISBN-based record. When those MARC records are treated as matches, they can overwrite more accurate or user-entered data. That reduces catalog reliability and causes data corruption.

The MARC import appears to be matching on title similarity alone, skipping deeper comparison or confidence thresholds, and then overwriting existing records.

- Update the `find_match` function in `openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py` to try `find_quick_match` first. If that finds no match, try `find_threshold_match`. If neither returns a match, return `None`.
- Update `editions_match` in `openlibrary/catalog/add_book/match.py` so author comparison aggregates authors from both the edition and its associated work.
- When using `find_threshold_match`, do not let records without an ISBN match existing records that only have a title and an ISBN unless the threshold confidence rule (`875`) is satisfied by enough supporting metadata, like matching authors or publish dates. Title alone is not enough in this case.
rephrased_fields.D:
Do not match MARC records with missing critical metadata to existing records based only on a title string, especially when the existing record includes an ISBN.

- The `test_noisbn_record_should_not_match_title_only()` function should verify that title-only matching does not produce a match.
rephrased_fields.R:
1- Trigger a MARC import that includes a record with a title matching an existing record but missing author, date, or ISBN information.

2- Make sure the existing record includes an ISBN and minimal but accurate metadata.

3- Check whether the MARC record is incorrectly matched and replaces or alters the existing one.
rephrased_fields.A: Check the different matching paths in the import flow. Some of them appear to skip robust threshold scoring and fall back to quick or exact title matching instead.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix Internet Archive imports in `get_ia_record()` so language and page count metadata get extracted correctly. Right now it misses or misreads language when IA sends full language names like "English" instead of 3-character codes, and it mishandles page count when that data needs to come from the `imagecount` field. That leaves imported books with missing or wrong language and page count data, which hurts search, display, and overall data quality. This can happen a lot depending on the IA metadata format.

- Add new exception classes named LanguageNoMatchError and LanguageMultipleMatchError for the cases where a full language name matches nothing or matches more than one language.

- Add a new helper function `get_abbrev_from_full_lang_name` to convert a full language name into its matching 3-character code. Make it raise LanguageNoMatchError when nothing matches, and LanguageMultipleMatchError when more than one match is found.

- When `get_abbrev_from_full_lang_name` raises LanguageNoMatchError or LanguageMultipleMatchError, make `get_ia_record` log a warning with `logger.warning`, and include both the language name and the record identifier from `metadata.get("identifier")` in the message.

- Update `get_ia_record` to handle full language names through `get_abbrev_from_full_lang_name`, leave edition language unset when the language cannot be resolved uniquely, and use `imagecount` from IA metadata to compute `number_of_pages` by subtracting 4 when the result is at least 1. If subtracting 4 would make the value less than 1, use the original `imagecount` as `number_of_pages` instead. Also make sure `number_of_pages` is never negative or zero.

- Keep warning logs and messages in the format: <WARNING_LEVEL> <MODULE>:<LINE_NUMBER> <Message>, and make the messages clearly distinguish between multiple language matches and no language matches.

- Make language handling work the same way for both full language names like "English" and 3-character codes like "eng".

- Make `get_ia_record` return a dictionary with title, authors, publisher, publish date, description, isbn, languages, subjects, and number of pages as keys.
rephrased_fields.D:
Implement a new utility function that converts full language names into 3-character codes and handles no-match and multiple-match cases with specific exceptions. Then update the main record import function to use that utility so language detection is reliable. Also update the import logic to derive page count correctly from the image count field and make sure the result is never less than 1.

- Make `get_abbrev_from_full_lang_name` normalize language names by stripping accents, converting to lowercase, and trimming whitespace.

- Make `get_abbrev_from_full_lang_name` check the canonical language name, translated names from `name_translated`, and alternative labels or identifiers like `alt_labels` when looking for a match.

- Make `get_languages` return a dictionary mapping language keys to language objects so code lookups are efficient.

- Make `autocomplete_languages` return an iterator of language objects, with each object exposing `key`, `code`, and `name` attributes.

- Use ISO-639-2/B bibliographic three-letter codes for stored and output language codes.
rephrased_fields.R: Try importing an Internet Archive record where the language metadata field contains a full language name like "French", "Frisian", or "English" instead of a 3-character ISO 639-2 code like "fre" or "eng". Also try importing an Internet Archive record where the `imagecount` metadata field is present and the book is very short, with values like 5, 4, or 3. Check the imported result. The book language can end up missing or wrong, and `number_of_pages` can be missing or calculated incorrectly, including negative values. Examples of IA records that previously triggered this: "Activity Ideas for the Budget Minded (activityideasfor00debr)" and "What's Great (whatsgreatphonic00harc)".
rephrased_fields.A: Apply this in the `get_ia_record()` function in openlibrary/plugins/importapi/code.py. This mainly affects imports that depend heavily on raw IA metadata instead of a MARC record. The root problem is weak parsing for language strings and missing robust handling of the `imagecount` field when deriving `number_of_pages`. Improve that extraction logic so imported book records are more complete and accurate.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix book imports hanging or timing out when processing cover images from unsupported hosts.

When `load()` imports books, including through `/isbn` or `/api/import`, a `cover` URL from a host that is not supported can make the import hang or time out. That happens because the HTTP proxy only allows certain cover image hosts. If the import tries to fetch a cover from a host outside that allow-list, it can time out and slow the whole import down.

This can happen any time a book import includes a cover URL pointing to an unsupported host.

Expected impact: delayed or failed imports because of timeouts.

Update the import flow so it does not try to fetch cover images from arbitrary hosts. Only process `cover` URLs whose host matches an entry in `ALLOWED_COVER_HOSTS`.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make the import only fetch cover images from allowed hosts and ignore unsupported ones so imports do not time out.

- Compare `cover` URL hostnames case-insensitively, and support both HTTP and HTTPS.
- If the `cover` field exists in an edition dictionary and the URL host does not match any entry in `ALLOWED_COVER_HOSTS`, ignore that cover URL and remove the `cover` key from the edition dictionary.
- If the `cover` URL host is in `ALLOWED_COVER_HOSTS`, extract the URL for later processing and remove the `cover` key from the edition dictionary.
- Implement the cover extraction and validation logic in a callable that takes the edition dictionary and the allowed hosts, and returns both the extracted cover URL (or `None`) and the updated edition dictionary with the `cover` key removed.
- Handle all input variations consistently: if `cover` is missing, return `None` and leave the edition unchanged; if `cover` is present but unsupported, return `None` and remove the key; if it is valid, return the URL and also remove the key. Hostname matching must stay case-insensitive and support both HTTP and HTTPS.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Import a book record through `/isbn` or `/api/import` that includes a `cover` URL whose host is not in the proxy allow-list.

2. Wait for the import to finish processing.
rephrased_fields.A: Define the allowed host list as the constant `ALLOWED_COVER_HOSTS` and use it everywhere in the relevant import logic.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix how Open Graph URLs and images get their host. Right now they resolve from the request host parameter.
When Navidrome runs behind nginx, nginx has to forward the Host header with `proxy_set_header Host $host;`. Only the `share` feature seems to depend on this, and that is not obvious unless you dig through the source.

<meta property\="og:url" content\="{{ .ShareURL }}"\> <meta property\="og:title" content\="{{ .ShareDescription }}"\> <meta property\="og:image" content\="{{ .ShareImageURL }}"\>
```

```

```

```

```
Notice that the Open Graph URL and image hostname end up matching the hostname used in the nginx proxy pass.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make the base path of `og:url` and `og:image` match the base path of the share URL.

- Support specifying the public base URL with the `BaseURL` key, and allow it to be either a path or a full URL. When it is a full URL, extract and store the scheme in `BaseScheme`, the host (including port if present) in `BaseHost`, and the path in `BasePath`.
- Add these fields to the server config object (`conf.Server`): `BaseScheme` (string), `BaseHost` (string), and `BasePath` (string).
- Use `BasePath` as the prefix for all routing and path-related operations, replacing any previous use of `BaseURL` for that purpose.
- Keep the `AbsoluteURL` function signature as `AbsoluteURL(r *http.Request, url string, params url.Values) string`, and build absolute URLs from the request, URL path, and query parameters.
- When generating absolute URLs for external use, like share links and Open Graph metadata such as `og:url` and `og:image`, use `BaseScheme` and `BaseHost` if they are set. If either is not set, fall back to the incoming request scheme and Host header.
- Handle both legacy configs where `BaseURL` is only a path and newer configs where `BaseURL` is a full URL, and make sure both produce correct URLs in headers, HTML metadata, and API responses.
- For any cookies set by the app, like auth or client identifier cookies, set the cookie `Path` to `BasePath` if it is set, otherwise `/`.
- Use `BasePath` as the prefix when mounting internal routers, serving static files, and registering HTTP handlers.
- When building URLs with extra query parameters, append and encode them correctly whether the config uses a base path or a full base URL.
- Expose the new config fields as `conf.Server.BaseScheme`, `conf.Server.BaseHost`, and `conf.Server.BasePath`, and use them anywhere public URL building, routing, or cookie path setup happens.
- Keep existing installs working without config changes when they only use a path in `BaseURL`, and keep routing, URL, and cookie behavior unchanged for them.
- Make `AbsoluteURL` treat any input URL that already has a scheme, such as “http://” or “https://”, as a fully formed URL. Do not override its scheme, host, or path. Still append query parameters.
- Update all existing references to `conf.Server.BaseURL` to use `conf.Server.BasePath`, and stop using `BaseURL` directly in route-building or absolute URL logic.

rephrased_fields.P:
Update the scanner to support R128 gain tags for track and album.

Right now the metadata scanner only reads `ReplayGain `tags for gain values. It ignores R128 gain tags (`r128_track_gain`, `r128_album_gain`), which are common in OPUS files. Because of that, files that only provide R128 tags end up showing missing or inconsistent gain in the app. Recognize both formats and keep the loudness reference consistent with the existing output.

- Support reading gain values from both ReplayGain tags (`replaygain_album_gain`, `replaygain_track_gain`) and R128 gain tags (`r128_album_gain`, `r128_track_gain`) for both album and track gain fields.

- If both ReplayGain and R128 tags exist for the same gain field, prefer the ReplayGain value. Only use R128 when ReplayGain is missing.

- Accept ReplayGain tag values as floating-point numbers expressed as text, with an optional “dB” suffix.

- Interpret R128 gain tag values as signed fixed-point numbers (Q7.8 format), normalized to match the loudness reference level expected from ReplayGain tags.

Spotify and Last.fm are both configured in Navidrome and working normally. DSub also works fine for top songs, similar artists, and artist biography.

This only showed up with these two artists so far:
-Billie Eilish
-Marilyn Manson

For "Billie Eilish", the result is "Biography not available", and none of the Last.fm top songs or similar artists work. For "Marilyn Manson", the Last.fm API returns the artist name as "unknown". Similar artists, radio, and top songs also do not work.

The music library was imported with beet using MusicBrainz or Discorgs, so the metadata is clean. Both `artist` and `albumartist` ID3 tag values are correct and match for both artists.

Airsonic and Airsonic-advanced were also checked for comparison. For both artists, DSub shows the correct behavior there.

Use the logs below as a reference. For example, the ArtistId for Marilyn Manson is `c34c29011299db886bee441c4a21874e`. Searching that in Google still resolves to "Marilyn Manson", so the correct artist is still being identified somewhere.

Make these code changes:

- The function `callArtistGetInfo` in `core/agents/lastfm.go` must retry the call with an empty `mbid` if the response does not contain an error but the returned artist information indicates an unknown result (specifically when the artist name equals "[unknown]"), or if the error is of type `*lastfm.Error` with code `6`, and must log a warning message before retrying that includes the artist name and original `mbid`.
- The function `callArtistGetSimilar` in `core/agents/lastfm.go` must retry the call with an empty `mbid` if the response does not contain an error but the returned artist information indicates an unknown result (specifically when the artist name equals "[unknown]"), or if the error is of type `*lastfm.Error` with code `6`, and must log a warning message before retrying that includes the artist name and original `mbid`; it must also be modified to return only the list of similar artists from the result object instead of the entire response wrapper.
- The function `callArtistGetTopTracks` in `core/agents/lastfm.go` must retry the call with an empty `mbid` if the response does not contain an error but the returned artist information indicates an unknown result (specifically when the artist name equals "[unknown]"), or if the error is of type `*lastfm.Error` with code `6`, and must log a warning message before retrying that includes the artist name and original `mbid`; it must also be modified to return only the list of top tracks from the result object instead of the entire response wrapper.
- The file `utils/lastfm/client.go` must define a new public error type named `Error` with fields `Code` (int) and `Message` (string), and implement the `Error()` method to return a formatted string describing the error that matches the pattern expected by error comparison tests.
- The function `makeRequest` in `utils/lastfm/client.go` must be modified to parse the response body into a `Response` object before checking the HTTP status code, and must return a generic error message with the status code if JSON parsing fails and the status code is not 200.
- The function `makeRequest` in `utils/lastfm/client.go` must be modified to return a typed `*Error` if the parsed `Response` object includes a non-zero error code, and must remove the existing call to the `parseError` function.
- The functions `ArtistGetSimilar` and `ArtistGetTopTracks` in `utils/lastfm/client.go` must be modified to return pointers to their respective wrapper objects (`*SimilarArtists` and `*TopTracks`) instead of returning slices of `Artist` or `Track` directly, with the wrapper objects containing an `Artists` field (slice of Artist) and a `Track` field (slice of Track) respectively.
- The private function `parseError` must be removed from `utils/lastfm/client.go`.
- The struct `Response` in `utils/lastfm/responses.go` must be extended to include two new fields, `Error` (int) and `Message` (string), to support structured error handling, and the previously defined `Error` struct must be removed.
- The structs `SimilarArtists` and `TopTracks` in `utils/lastfm/responses.go` must be extended to include a new metadata field of type `Attr`, and a new struct `Attr` must be defined with a single field named `Artist` of type `string`.
- All retry logic must ensure that the second call (without MBID) uses an empty string for the MBID parameter, which can be verified by checking that `URL.Query().Get("mbid")` returns an empty string in test scenarios.
- The error handling must distinguish between Last.fm API errors (which should trigger retries for code 6) and other HTTP or parsing errors (which should not trigger retries).

Preserve existing images, biographies, and tags when they already exist.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix local SSO URL rewriting for the local proxy setup.

When the app runs under a `*.proton.local` host, some service URLs still get generated as `*.proton.black`. That breaks the local proxy setup. Add a rewrite that only runs in local-sso environments and converts incoming URLs to the right `*.proton.local` domain and port. Leave every other environment unchanged.
rephrased_fields.D:
- When the current host ends with `.proton.local`, rewrite any `*.proton.black` URL to the matching `*.proton.local` URL. Preserve the subdomain and the current port.  

- When the current host is not under `.proton.local` (for example, `localhost` or `proton.me`), leave the URL unchanged.

- Keep the rewrite conditional. Only activate it when the current browser hostname ends with proton.local. In every other environment, like localhost or proton.me, return the input URL unchanged.  
- Replace only the host component so it matches the local-sso proxy. Preserve the original scheme, path, query parameters, and fragment exactly as provided.  
- Preserve the port by applying the current page port to the rewritten host when a port is present, so requests go through the same local proxy port. For example, if the current page is drive.proton.local:8888 and the input URL host is drive.proton.black, return drive.proton.local:8888 with the same path, query, and fragment.  
- Use the leftmost label of the input hostname as the service identifier for subdomain mapping. For example, rewrite `drive.env.proton.black` to `drive.proton.local` with the correct port, and rewrite `drive-api.proton.black` to `drive-api.proton.local` with the correct port.  
- Keep the behavior idempotent. If the input already targets proton.local, with or without a port, return it unchanged.  
- Make behavior deterministic for inputs under the proton.black base domain by converting them to the matching proton.local base domain and applying the rules above.  
- Preserve hyphenated subdomains exactly. For example, rewrite `drive-api.proton.black` to `drive-api.proton.local` with the correct port.  
- For multi-label subdomains with environment labels like `drive.env` or `drive-api.env`, rewrite them to the matching service subdomain without the environment label, producing `drive.proton.local` or `drive-api.proton.local` with the correct port.  
- Ensure the function only operates on absolute URLs. If the input string is not a valid absolute URL, throw the standard TypeError produced by the URL constructor. Do not silently rewrite, ignore, or return malformed values.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Open the app in a browser with a host under `*.proton.local` (for example, `https://drive.proton.local:8888`).  

2. Use any service URL that points to `*.proton.black`.  

3. Check the resolved URL the app uses.
rephrased_fields.A: - In local-sso, `.proton.black` URLs are used as-is, and they do not match the `*.proton.local` domain or port. That makes them incompatible with the proxy setup.

rephrased_fields.P:
`ModalTwo` tests break because JSDOM doesn’t handle `<dialog>` properly.

When `ModalTwo` renders in JSDOM, incomplete `HTMLDialogElement` support stops the dialog from acting like a real modal container: JSDOM can’t reliably traverse the `<dialog>`, elements inside it are hard to find with DOM queries, and role-based queries like `getByRole` fail to find expected children even when the dialog is open.

This makes automated `ModalTwo` tests fail in CI and locally, blocks accessibility assertions from finding dialog content, and creates false negatives that slow down feedback.

- Add a Dialog abstraction component that wraps native <dialog> behavior so callers don’t have to mount a native <dialog> directly.
- Update ModalTwo to use the Dialog abstraction for its modal container instead of instantiating a native <dialog> directly.
- In environments where HTMLDialogElement is missing or limited, make the Dialog component fall back to a compatible host element without throwing, while preserving aria attributes and keeping children present and accessible.
- Let the Dialog component swap implementations per environment, for example through module aliasing or dependency injection, so non-browser or limited DOM environments can provide an alternative host element.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make `ModalTwo` expose its children in the accessible tree during JSDOM-based tests whenever it renders with `open`, so queries like `getByRole('button', { name: 'Hello' })` succeed consistently. Make the tests pass deterministically without needing a real browser environment.

- Make the Dialog component provide an element reference to the underlying dialog host so callers can invoke standard dialog operations when supported.
- Make the Dialog component accept and forward standard HTMLDialogElement attributes plus any aria-* or data-* attributes to its host element.
- Render children unchanged so interactive descendants keep their roles, semantics, and tab order.
- Forward props and the element reference consistently to the rendered host no matter whether it uses a native dialog or a fallback.
- Make sure the rendered ModalTwo markup with the Dialog abstraction keeps interactive children discoverable by accessibility role and still operable.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Render `<ModalTwo open>` in a JSDOM-based test.

2. Include an interactive child element (e.g., `<Button>Hello</Button>`).

3. Query the child by role using Testing Library.

4. Observe that the element is not found or is reported as not visible.
rephrased_fields.A: In JSDOM, `<dialog>` doesn’t expose its contents in a way that works with role-based queries, so tests fail even when the component is open and its children are present.

rephrased_fields.P:
Make the ELF parser safely handle file read and seek failures.

Update the parser so read and seek operations don't fail unclearly. Right now, some file operations can raise unhandled errors, and there’s no debug log when parsing succeeds. Fix that to make parsing more reliable.

If a file read or seek fails with `OSError` or `OverflowError`, raise a parsing error instead of letting it fail in an unclear way. Also, always write a debug log message that confirms success and includes the detected versions.

- If reading from or seeking in the ELF file fails with `OSError` or `OverflowError`, raise a `ParseError`.

- When parsing invalid, malformed, or truncated ELF data, only ever raise a `ParseError`. Do not crash or raise any other exception type.

- During a successful parse via `parse_webenginecore()`, emit exactly one log record in total, and make sure it starts with "Got versions from ELF:".

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix the slowdown when adding configurations with URL patterns at scale.

Adding or updating a lot of URL-pattern-scoped configurations gets linearly slower and starts blocking bulk operations. With hundreds or thousands of entries, batch inserts become impractical and can end up causing long delays, timeouts, or hangs.
rephrased_fields.D:
Make adding and managing configurations with URL patterns efficient and stable at large scale (thousands of entries), without hangs or timeouts during insert/update operations.

- Make the `Values(opt, values=...)` constructor accept a `ScopedValue` sequence and load it with the same effect and order as calling `add` for each element in that order.
- Expose a `values._vmap` attribute whose iteration order matches insertion order; the sequence from `iter(values)` must exactly match `list(values._vmap.values())`.
- Make “normal” iteration list the global value first (if any, `pattern=None`) and then the specific values in insertion order.
- Make `repr(values)` include `opt={!r}` and return the state using a `vmap=` key whose contents are printed as `odict_values([ScopedValue(...), ...])`, in the same order as the iteration.
- Make `str(values)` produce lines in “normal” order; for the global: `"<opt.name> = <value_str>"`; for each pattern: `"<opt.name>['<pattern_str>'] = <value_str>"`; if there are no values, `"<opt.name>: <unchanged>"`.
- Make `bool(values)` return `True` when at least one `ScopedValue` exists and `False` when none do.
- Make `add(value, pattern)` create a new entry when one doesn't exist and replace the existing one when there is already a value for that `pattern`, while keeping uniqueness per pattern.
- Make `remove(pattern)` remove the entry exactly associated with `pattern` and return `True` if it deleted something; if no such entry exists, return `False`.
- Make `clear()` remove all customizations (global and pattern), leaving the collection empty.
- Make `get_for_url(url, ...)` return the value whose pattern matches `url`, giving precedence to the most recently added value; if there are no matches, use the global value if it exists, or apply the established fallback behavior.
- Make `get_for_pattern(pattern, fallback=...)` return the exact pattern value if it exists; if it does not exist and `fallback=False`, return `UNSET`; if fallback is allowed, apply the global value or the default policy.
- Make operations that accept a non-null `pattern` validate that the associated option supports patterns before operating.
- Make sure bulk insertion of thousands of patterned entries does not cause exceptions, hangs, or timeouts in the test environment; the addition benchmark must complete successfully.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Prepare a list of ≥1000 configurations with URL patterns.

2. Add them in batch or repeatedly call `values.add(...)`.

3. Observe the high latency and, in extreme cases, timeouts or hangs.
rephrased_fields.A: This hits users and automations that apply rules at large scale, like big host lists.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix a crash on Qt 6, especially under Wayland, where some hardware/system events like plugging or unplugging power or pressing special keys such as “Airplane mode” come through as `QKeyEvent` with `e.key() == 0` (unknown key). Right now, code that does `Qt.Key(e.key())` raises `ValueError: 0 is not a valid Qt.Key`, which crashes qutebrowser. Key handling is also duplicated across multiple call sites, so centralize it to safely reject unknown keys and to keep “special” and modifier logic consistent.
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
File "qutebrowser/keyinput/basekeyparser.py", line 284, in handle
key = Qt.Key(e.key())
...
ValueError: 0 is not a valid Qt.Key```

- Stop constructing `Qt.Key` from raw integers in all key-event handling, and call `KeyInfo.from_event(e)` instead.
- Make `KeyInfo.from_event(e)` validate the event and raise `InvalidKeyError` for unknown or invalid codes, including `0`.
- Make all parsers and handlers catch `InvalidKeyError`, log a debug message to the `keyboard` logger, and return `QKeySequence.SequenceMatch.NoMatch`.
- Make sure a synthesized `QKeyEvent` with `e.key() == 0` never crashes and gets ignored with only a debug log entry.
rephrased_fields.D:
- Add `KeyInfo.is_special(self) -> bool` and make it return `True` when the key needs special binding syntax, and `False` for printable keys with only `Shift` or no modifiers.
- Add `KeyInfo.is_modifier_key(self) -> bool` and make it return `True` for keys listed in `_MODIFIER_MAP`, and `False` otherwise.
- Make `KeyInfo.__str__` decide formatting through `self.is_special()` and stop calling removed free functions.
- Keep behavior for valid keys and modifiers identical on Qt 5/6 and on X11/Wayland.
rephrased_fields.R:
1. Run qutebrowser on Qt 6 / Wayland.
2. Trigger a hardware or special key event that produces an unknown key code, for example plugging in power or pressing an “Airplane mode” key.
3. Observe the crash caused by `ValueError` when code constructs `Qt.Key(e.key())`.
rephrased_fields.A:
- Stop using the free functions `keyutils.is_special` and `keyutils.is_modifier_key` in production code.
- Update unit tests to use `KeyInfo(...).is_special()` and `KeyInfo(...).is_modifier_key()`, and remove references to the deleted free functions.

rephrased_fields.P:
Fix the offline login edge case. After logging in while offline, the app can end up with an `accessToken` but without the encryption keys it needs. The app sends API requests, then fails when it tries to decrypt the result.
